issues.description: OutputImageRawFrame is constructed with format='RGB' but image.tobytes() reflects the source mode, which may be RGBA or P
issues.detail: PIL.Image.open infers the mode from the decoded bytes (PNG from Gemini can be RGBA or palette). Calling image.tobytes() returns bytes in that native mode, while the frame declares format='RGB'. Downstream consumers will misinterpret stride and channel count, producing color-shifted or corrupted output. Convert explicitly: image = image.convert('RGB') before tobytes().

issues.description: Mutating genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE at import time is a global, undocumented side effect
issues.detail: The 'temporary hack' reaches into a private module attribute of google-genai and rewrites it for every consumer of the library in the process. This is fragile across the >=1.41,<2 range you just opened, and the chosen 5 MiB constant has no stated invariant or measurement. State why 5 MiB, or scope the override to the client instance, or upstream a fix.

issues.description: Image emission loop has no stated invariant about ordering or pairing with text parts
issues.detail: Inside _process_context, parts are iterated and inline_data images are push_frame'd inline with text and function-call handling. There is no comment stating the invariant: are images expected before, after, or interleaved with LLMTextFrames in the same turn? Aggregators and the assistant context downstream depend on this ordering; document it or a future maintainer will reorder by accident.

issues.description: Image-model detection by substring 'image' in model name is brittle
issues.detail: _maybe_unset_thinking_budget uses `if 'image' in self._model_name` to gate behavior. This is a stringly-typed predicate that will misfire on any future model whose name happens to contain the substring (or fail to fire if Google renames). A small explicit set of image-capable model prefixes, or a capability flag, would be both more readable and more auditable.

issues.description: No literate comment explains why the default model was changed from 2.0-flash to 2.5-flash
issues.detail: The default flips silently in __init__ and the CHANGELOG notes the change in one line. A reader auditing behavioral regressions (thinking budget defaults, cost, latency) gets no in-code rationale. A short comment above the default, or a docstring note, would make the choice survivable for future maintainers.

issues.description: No test or example assertion verifies the image-emission path
issues.detail: The new example wires a pipeline but does not assert that OutputImageRawFrames are produced or correctly formatted. Per the maxim: proofs and tests complement each other. At minimum a unit test feeding a fake candidate with inline_data through _process_context and asserting the emitted frame's size, format, and bytes-length would catch the format='RGB' issue above.

review.summary: The PR adds a clean, narrow extension point for image-returning Gemini models, and the surface area is small. The algorithmic core, however, is UNDER-AUDITED: the frame's declared format='RGB' is asserted without converting the PIL image to RGB first, which will silently corrupt RGBA/palette PNGs that Gemini does return. A global mutation of a private google-genai buffer constant is labeled a 'hack' in the code itself and deserves either a measurement-backed justification or a scoped fix. Smaller concerns: substring-based model detection, an undocumented default-model change, and no test exercising the new branch. Fix the format conversion before merge; the rest is literate-comment and rigor debt.
